anchor_evidence: Chose 'running my own book of work, even if smaller' over a bigger corporate mandate, and said the WMS cutover was the last time he felt fully in charge of an outcome.
flow_sources: untangling a messy operation and re-mapping the whole flow end-to-end
walking a new supervisor through the floor until the process finally clicks for them
preparing for a carrier negotiation — building the cost model and playing out counters
energy_drains: constant new-client hunting — cold outreach and always having to sell himself to strangers

hidden_strengths.strength: Developing juniors into confident supervisors — structured, patient teaching that sticks
hidden_strengths.why_hidden: The CV frames it as operational output (a training curriculum, audit passes) rather than a personal capability; he doesn't think of teaching as a skill because it 'came with the job'.
hidden_strengths.evidence: When asked when he last lost track of time at work, he described onboarding two new supervisors during the WMS migration — not the migration itself.

stated_vs_demonstrated_tension: He says he wants out of big-company structure, but every story he lights up telling is about building structure — SOPs, curricula, audit regimes. The pull is toward owning the system he builds, not escaping systems.
